actualAttackCounterexample.fixtureControl: Weakness Guard Energy on Aerodactyl keeps it alive for both legitimate attacks, without editing printed metadata.

cardContractVerified: Monkey Trio requires exactly Simisage, Simisear and Simipour in play on its owner side; removes only Colorless costs and is suppressed independently.
Copying Arm Thrust Needle does not copy Monkey Trio or grant permission to use it.
Self-protection belongs to the physical attacking or copied Pokémon and does not test its own Ability permission.
Protection expires at the end of the opponent turn and is removed by switching; copying source removal does not remove the copy user protection.
Protection survives full StateSerializer roundtrip, including copied checkpoint restoration; reset removes the protection and old copied sessions.
Only ordinary attack damage is prevented; poison and damage counters remain effective.
The physical attacking Pokémon named Simisage is excepted, regardless of selected/copied attack source.
Used VSTAR Abilities remain Abilities; Pokémon Powers are not Abilities.

sharedBlockers.problem: The current CheckPokemonPowersEffect aliases target.powers; Tool/LV.X/gained-power queries can mutate intrinsic definition data.
sharedBlockers.evidence: red-results.json: ordinary usable-power UI query mutation

sharedBlockers.problem: The usable-power query adds Tool powers. Official rules distinguish being able to use a Tool Ability from the Pokémon having that Ability.
sharedBlockers.prototypeMitigation: Explicit includeToolPowers=false mode; insufficient on its own if earlier ordinary query already polluted card.powers.

sharedBlockers.problem: Galarian Weezing and Iron Thorns implement ability-use rejection but not effective-power removal queries.
Ancient Star grants an Ability in card text, but does not add it to effective-power query.
Single-pass query is traversal-order dependent: a remover can filter powers before Unown appends Star Cipher, leaving a gained Ability present under Garbotoxin.
sharedBlockers.evidence: red-results.json: gained Ability remains removed independent of fan-out order

recommendedIncrementalSequence: First isolate queried power arrays from immutable card definitions, with regression tests for ordinary UI and repeated Tool/gained-power queries.
Define an explicit intrinsic-Ability presence query distinct from activation permission and Tool usability; collect intrinsic printed, inherited and genuinely gained powers before applying removal.
Audit removal producers one at a time with ownership, Ability Shield/Stadium immunity, suppression, source-zone and exception tests; missing adapters must remain visible failures.
Once that contract is reliable, revisit this attack-owned Simisage candidate and rerun direct/copy/restore/reset tests plus saved-state/action corpus against the then-current shared tree.
limitations: No claim that all legacy Ability removers or inherited/gained powers have been exhaustively audited.
IS_ABILITY_BLOCKED remains appropriate for Monkey Trio permission but is not used as an attacker-has-Ability predicate.
General stale source/target slot reuse and broader movement lifecycle proposals remain outside this isolated investigation.
Existing saved-state/action corpus was not rerun because integration is blocked; eight recorded real puzzle wins are compatibility smoke evidence only.
No app bundle, metadata generator, deployment or shared runtime source was changed.
